topLine: NSW politics was dominated by the Minns government's decision to legislate for increased coal production at the Mount Pleasant mine in the Upper Hunter, announced as a response to a High Court ruling and framed by the Premier as protecting 400 jobs — a move environment groups describe as overreach. Elsewhere, the Opposition leader attacked the gun buyback scheme and the government continued announcements on hospitals, childcare and Sydney waterfront planning. Locally, Kiama Council is weighing a 20 per cent rate rise to close a $3.8 million deficit, and Shoalhaven Hospital's $440 million building is due to open on 28 October.

Elsewhere, the Opposition leader attacked the gun buyback scheme and the government continued announcements on hospitals, childcare and Sydney waterfront planning. briefing.localWatch: Kiama ratepayers face a possible 20 per cent rate increase, with councillors warning the alternative is service cuts, while Shoalhaven Hospital prepares to open its $440 million wing on 28 October. A Greens candidate has also launched a campaign centred on Nowra rents and homelessness, an early marker for the 2027 South Coast contest.

stories.headline: Pay up or lose services: Kiama ratepayers face new household budget hit in council ultimatum
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Kiama Council is considering lifting rates by 20 per cent to wipe out a $3.8 million deficit. According to the report, councillors have warned that cuts to local services are the alternative.

stories.headline: What Shoalhaven's new $440m healthcare hub means for local families and kids
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports Shoalhaven Hospital will open its $440 million building on 28 October, with new emergency facilities and services the paper describes as regional firsts intended to reduce patient waiting times.

stories.headline: Shocking discovery in public toilet sparks passionate fight for South Coast
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports Greens candidate Kim Stephenson is campaigning on housing, pointing to weekly rents of around $600 and people sleeping rough in Nowra, and calling for an overhaul of state housing policy.

stories.headline: Gerringong SLSC long-term lease close to being finalised
stories.summary: Kiama Council says a long-term lease for the Gerringong Surf Life Saving Club is close to being finalised, according to a notice published on the council's website.

stories.headline: Nowra and Milton showground changes open for feedback
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council has opened a public consultation on proposed changes at the Nowra and Milton showgrounds, according to a council notice.

stories.headline: ‘Hold on to your guns’: NSW Opposition leader says gun buyback scheme targets ‘wrong enemy’
stories.summary: 7NEWS reports the NSW Opposition leader has criticised the gun buyback scheme, saying it targets the "wrong enemy". In a related report, 7NEWS says the Opposition leader has backed a boycott of the buyback.

stories.headline: Greens mining ‘for dirt’ in a rush for the courts
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports on a dispute over the Greens' use of parliamentary powers in relation to coal litigation in NSW. Only the headline was available in the supplied material.

stories.headline: NSW government drafts law to allow Upper Hunter mine to increase output
stories.summary: Premier Chris Minns says the government will introduce legislation in the next sitting fortnight to allow MACH Energy's Mount Pleasant coal mine in the Hunter to lift production, with the stated aim of protecting 400 jobs through to 2032. The SMH reports the bill would permit an increase of four million tonnes a year, while the Guardian reports the mine's expansion was subject to a recent High Court decision and that critics have called the bill "legislative overreach"; the ABC reports environment leaders describe the move as government overreach. The AFR reports Minns has described the measure as a single-use solution and warned other resources companies not to expect a legislative fix if courts reject their proposals.

stories.headline: $400 million for hospitals following mould scandal exposure
stories.summary: The Newcastle Herald reports Premier Chris Minns has committed $400 million in the budget for hospitals following the mould issues reported at the Calvary Mater in Newcastle. The paper reports comment from Health Minister Ryan Park and Sarah Mitchell.

stories.headline: More childcare places and fairer pay - Minns Labor Government reforms of early learning sector continue
stories.summary: The NSW Government says its reforms to the early learning sector are continuing, pointing to additional childcare places and pay changes, according to a ministerial release.

stories.headline: The architects fighting to design a ‘distinctly Sydney’ waterfront suburb
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports the NSW government wants to make a bold claim on the transformation of an industrial port into a new suburb above the future Bays West metro station.

stories.headline: Judge finds Aboriginal protection order on goldmine 'fundamentally flawed'
stories.summary: The ABC reports the Federal Court has identified what it describes as fundamental flaws in the process that led to Aboriginal protection being granted over part of a goldmine site in NSW.

stories.headline: Six-year plastics factory fight takes toll on Moss Vale residents
stories.summary: The ABC reports residents have told the NSW Land and Environment Court that the long-running dispute over a recycling plant at Moss Vale is affecting their health and retirement plans, with the sustained uncertainty taking a psychological toll.

stories.headline: Sydney councillor resigns from Hunter's Hill Council over 'toxic chamber'
stories.summary: The ABC reports councillor Marc Lane has resigned from Hunter's Hill Council, saying he could not serve out his term on the Liberal-dominated council and citing what he described as a lack of debate over key decisions.

stories.headline: Tribunal quashes council's over-55s caravan park plans
stories.summary: The ABC reports a tribunal has ruled that a NSW council's move to bar anyone under 55 from living permanently at its caravan park had no "clear or coherent purpose".

stories.headline: Here's why Wollongong residents won't face a rate rise next year
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Wollongong residents will not face a rate rise next year. Only the headline was available in the supplied material.

stories.headline: Minns invokes One Nation to back coal jobs over climate targets
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald examines the Premier's framing of coal jobs against climate targets, reporting that NSW has approved 14 coal mine expansions or extensions since the March 2023 election and refused none, with another 17 in the pipeline.

stories.headline: Cheaper public transport just the ticket for voters
stories.summary: AAP News considers the politics of an election promise to cap weekly public transport fares, reporting that while the idea may appeal to voters, it raises questions about whether people outside the cities would benefit.

elsewhere.text: Independent Indi MP Helen Haines remains in a critical condition after what the ABC reports was an "attack" near her electorate office in north-east Victoria; the Prime Minister says counter-terrorism police are investigating and a man has been arrested.
